findings.summary:
Regression from R2-2 (D829): a straight closer now takes the glyph of a curly ‘ or ‚ that is really a wrong-way apostrophe (the Word/Google Docs autocorrect error: ‘90s, ‘80s, ‘til, ‘em, ‘cause, Dutch ‘s avonds, German ‚n, ‚90ern) or an unclosed curly scare quote inside a quotation the author opened with a straight mark. The outer quotation is left open, so every later quotation in the paragraph drops a level, and some pairs no longer match (en-GB single-outer typed “…’, nb «…’). en-US

"Back in the ‘90s we had fun," she said. "Yes," he said.

→

“Back in the ‘90s we had fun,’ she said. ‘Yes,’ he said.

(9822af0: “…fun,” she said. “Yes,” he said.). The same holds in en-GB, en-GB single-outer, da, de, es, nb, nl double-outer and pt, typed and depth alike. It also comes through Lite’s |sorts filter in the testbed. The SPEC’s own reason for narrowing D829 (“He’s from the ’hood” pushing every later quotation down a level) comes back as soon as the mark is curly:

"He’s from the ‘hood," she said. "Yes," he said.

→ “He’s from the ‘hood,’ she said. ‘Yes,’ he said.

findings.summary:
Regression from R2-1 against 9822af0: in fi and sv, the same-glyph pair counts any of its marks still to come, so a straight " or ' after a digit that really ends a curly ”…” or ’…’ becomes a prime whenever another quotation follows in the same paragraph. sv

”Det kostar 5", sa han. ”Billigt.”

→ 5″ (9822af0 5”); sv

”Det är rum 101", sa hon, ”eller 102”.

→ 101″; fi

”Se maksoi 5", hän sanoi. ”Halpa.”

→ 5″. These match c3b3b49, so they are no worse than base, but they are worse than 9822af0. R2-1’s clause that the real closer still closes is pinned only where nothing follows (”Det är 5").
